name: Bleeding Diathesis Due to Thromboxane Synthesis Deficiency

criteria.description: Recurrent mucocutaneous bleeding episodes including epistaxis and easy bruising
Abnormal platelet aggregation response to arachidonic acid with normal response to other agonists
Reduced or absent thromboxane A2 synthesis in platelet assays
Identification of mutations in thromboxane synthase gene (TBXAS1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent mucocutaneous bleeding plus abnormal platelet aggregation to arachidonic acid and reduced thromboxane A2 synthesis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on specialized platelet function testing and exclusion of other platelet function disorders.

searchTerms: repeated spontaneous bleeding from skin and mucous membranes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding time with normal platelet count
searchTerms: long bleeding time despite normal platelet number
prolonged bleeding with normal platelet count
extended bleeding time without low platelets

occasional.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after minor cuts or dental procedures
searchTerms: bleeding longer after small cuts or dental work

rare.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
searchTerms: low red blood cells from ongoing blood loss

laboratory: Abnormal platelet aggregation response to arachidonic acid
Reduced thromboxane B2 levels in urine or platelet assays
imaging: Imaging may reveal hemorrhagic complications such as intracranial bleeding in severe cases
other: Normal platelet morphology on blood smear

distinguishingFeatures: Absent platelet aggregation with multiple agonists including ADP and collagen
Deficiency or dysfunction of platelet integrin αIIbβ3
History of aspirin or NSAID use
Reversible platelet dysfunction upon drug withdrawal
Abnormal platelet aggregation with multiple agonists

redFlags: Unexplained prolonged bleeding after minor trauma or surgery
Persistent mucocutaneous bleeding refractory to standard hemostatic measures
references: Orphanet: Bleeding Diathesis Due to Thromboxane Synthesis Deficiency, ORPHA:220443
